compute.note: parameters evaluated from the stated architecture: FastLSTMNet, layers = 2, features = [16, 2] (the last layer has hilbert.local_size = 2 features), real float32 parameters. Each LSTM layer l has a kernel (in_l + n_prev f_l) x 4 f_l and a bias 4 f_l, with in_0 = 1 (the spin at the previous site), in_1 = 16, and n_prev = 1 previous neighbours per site: NetKet orders the 20 sites of the graph vmc.py builds (nk.graph.Grid([20], pbc=True)) greedily and takes the median number of earlier neighbours, rounded up (median 1; evaluated here by re-implementing ordering.py, not by running NetKet). So (1 + 1*16)*64 + 64 = 1152 and (16 + 1*2)*8 + 8 = 152, total 1304. samples = 1024 per optimisation step (MCState n_samples = batch_size; ARDirectSampler (autoregressive, one pass per sample)); iterations = 100000 (--max_step 100000); optimizer Adam, lr 1e-3. The final energy is then estimated once with estim_size = 1024^2 = 1048576 samples (not an optimisation step). NetKet pinned twice by the program: programs/vmc_netket/requirements.txt "NetKet==3.13.0" and conda_env.yaml "netket=3.11.4"; every NetKet line cited here reads the same at both tags. compute.note: Parameters evaluated: NetKet 3.13.0 Jastrow stores the strictly lower triangle of W, N(N-1)/2 = 20*19/2 = 190 real (float32) weights, which is also what vmc.py prints as n_params (tree_size_real_nonzero). Samples: 1024 per SR step, 1024 chains of length 1, each sample one sweep of 20 exchange proposals, no discard. Iterations: 10^4 steps (--max_step default). Driver: nk.VMC with nk.optimizer.SR(QGTOnTheFly) (n_parameters < n_samples). After training the energy is estimated from 2^20 samples. stored sigma 0.00049 vs sqrt(stored variance 0.2419342 / 2^20) = 0.00048: consistent with the script's 2^20-sample final estimate (--estim_size default). Provenance: the value entered VarBench in af1d48f (2022-09-01, Dian Wu); the linked script was added to varbench/methods in c686621 (2024-07-30) without the value changing, so the script is the authors' later reconstruction of the baseline, not a log of the run (the same holds for the TFIsing RBM rows, scripts/defects.mjs). The 2^20-sample final estimate is corroborated by the stored sigma; batch size and step count are not independently corroborated. No device or time is recorded (the conda env includes CUDA; the README says a GPU is "usually needed for VMC on larger lattices", which is not a statement about these runs). || pass 2026-09-27: evaluation from the script's code path. proposals_per_sample = N x (s + d)/s = 20 x (1 + 0)/1 = 20: batch 1024 = n_samples = n_chains (one sample per chain per step), n_discard_per_chain = 0, sweep_size = hilbert.size = N (NetKet default, every proposal a full forward). sr: n_parameters = 190 < n_samples = 1024, so nk.VMC with SR(QGTOnTheFly(), solver=solve); solve() calls A.to_dense(), which applies the lazy S to the P = 190 unit vectors (P jvp + transpose mat-vecs over all 1024 samples per step): kind onthefly_dense (verify/agent-A.md item 1: 3.9-23x the network count for the 26 rows with P < 1024). complex false: --dtype default float32, param_dtype=args.dtype, no script overrides it. local_energy all: NetKet's get_conn_padded; the NetKet LocalOperator pads to the batch maximum of nonzero elements, so on Heisenberg/J1-J2 'all' overstates the local energy by about 10-30 % (verify/agent-A.md item 4).
